title: simulated-user persona+goal task sets (branch coverage across 5 flow types)
description: Persona+goal tasks that drive an LLM simulated user through flow-enabled agents. Each type spans happy-path AND edges so the sessions exercise every branch the declared flow can take. The engine (tau2.flow.simulate) creates a throwaway agent of the type supplying NO flow (default flow auto-attaches, enabled), drives a full simulated conversation, then audits the trace vs the declared flow. Turn budgets are per-flow: 'max_turns' may be declared at the top level (global fallback), per type block (per-agent default sized to that flow's length), and per task (scenario override) — most specific wins. 'post_goal_turns' (same resolution) is the cooperative allowance the sim grants AFTER its goal is met for the agent to deliver its closing.

dental_receptionist.system_prompt: You are a dental clinic receptionist. Follow the current conversation-flow state instructions exactly and only use the tools you are permitted in the current state.

tasks.persona: Priya Nair, a new patient, calm and cooperative, has flexible mornings this week.
tasks.goal: Book a routine dental cleaning for a weekday morning as a new patient. Give your name and preferred day when asked and confirm the first suitable slot offered.

tasks.persona: Rahul Mehta, existing patient, busy professional who can only do late afternoons.
tasks.goal: Book a check-up but insist you can ONLY come after 4pm on a weekday; accept the first after-4pm slot offered and confirm.

tasks.persona: Anita Desai, existing patient with an appointment this Thursday she can no longer make.
tasks.goal: Reschedule your existing Thursday appointment to next Monday. Provide identifying details when asked and confirm the new time.

tasks.persona: Sameer Kapoor, existing patient, indecisive.
tasks.goal: Start trying to reschedule your appointment, then partway through decide you'd rather just cancel it entirely. Follow whatever the agent needs to cancel.

tasks.persona: Meera Iyer, existing patient, polite but firm.
tasks.goal: Cancel your upcoming dental appointment because you'll be travelling. Provide your name/details and confirm the cancellation.

tasks.persona: Vikram Rao, existing patient, terse, doesn't want to explain.
tasks.goal: Cancel your appointment. If asked why, say you'd rather not say. Still get it cancelled.

tasks.persona: Deepa Menon, new patient who can ONLY do this specific Saturday at 8am and nothing else.
tasks.goal: Try to book for Saturday 8am only. If that exact slot isn't available, decline every alternative and end the call without booking.

tasks.persona: Karthik S, prospective patient, just gathering info.
tasks.goal: Ask only for the clinic's opening hours and location. Do NOT book anything; thank them and hang up once you have the hours.

tasks.persona: Nisha Gupta, confused patient who first gives the wrong appointment date, then corrects herself.
tasks.goal: Reschedule your appointment, but first state the wrong day, then when the agent can't find it, correct yourself to the right day and complete the reschedule.

tasks.persona: Arjun Pillai, in pain with a possible broken tooth, anxious and wants the earliest possible visit.
tasks.goal: Explain you have severe tooth pain and need the earliest emergency appointment today. Accept the soonest slot offered.

tasks.persona: Lakshmi R, wants to leave a message for a specific hygienist.
tasks.goal: Ask to leave a message for the hygienist about a follow-up question; provide a callback number when asked and confirm the message was taken.

car_rental.system_prompt: You are a car rental booking agent. Follow the current conversation-flow state instructions exactly and only use the tools you are permitted in the current state.

tasks.persona: Jordan Lee, leisure traveller, easy-going, wants an SUV for a road trip.

tasks.persona: Sana Malik, budget-conscious solo traveller.
tasks.goal: Book the cheapest economy car for a 3-day weekend rental. Confirm the first economy option offered.

tasks.persona: Tom Becker, needs a specific rare vehicle (a convertible) on a peak holiday weekend.
tasks.goal: Ask to rent a convertible for this coming holiday weekend. If none are available, decline substitutes and end the call without booking.

tasks.persona: Grace Kim, starts wanting a sedan then upgrades her mind mid-call.
tasks.goal: Begin booking a sedan, then partway through change to wanting an SUV instead. Complete the booking for the SUV.

tasks.persona: Malik Ahmed, comparison shopper, not ready to commit.
tasks.goal: Ask about pricing and what vehicle classes are available, but do NOT book anything. Thank them and end the call once you have the info.

tasks.persona: Elena Petrova, relocating, needs a car for a full month.
tasks.goal: Book a mid-size car for a one-month rental. Provide start date and duration and confirm.

tasks.persona: Dev Sharma, needs a one-way rental between two cities.
tasks.goal: Book a one-way rental picking up in one city and dropping off in another. Ask if one-way is possible and, if so, complete the booking.

tasks.persona: Chloe Martin, wants to add a second driver to the booking.

tasks.persona: Ryan Cole, gets sticker shock at the quoted price.
tasks.goal: Try to book an SUV, but when you hear the price react that it's too expensive and decline to book. End the call without a reservation.

tasks.persona: Fatima Noor, confused about her travel dates, gives a past date first.
tasks.goal: Try to book a car but first give a pickup date that's in the past; when corrected, give a valid future date and complete the booking.

tasks.persona: Marcus Webb, celebrating an anniversary, wants a premium car.
tasks.goal: Book a luxury/premium vehicle for a weekend. Ask what premium options exist and confirm the one offered.

debt_collection.system_prompt: You are a debt-collection agent. You MUST verify the caller's identity per your flow before disclosing ANY account, balance, or debt details. Follow the current conversation-flow state instructions exactly and only use the tools you are permitted in the current state.

tasks.persona: the correct debtor, John Miller, cooperative and ready to settle.
tasks.goal: You ARE the right party. Confirm your identity when asked (name/DOB/last-4 as requested), then agree to pay the balance in full today.

tasks.persona: the correct debtor, Sarah Owens, wants to pay but not today.
tasks.goal: Verify your identity, then instead of paying now, promise to pay on a specific date two weeks out. Get that promise-to-pay recorded.

tasks.persona: the correct debtor, Alan Pierce, who believes the debt is wrong.
tasks.goal: Verify your identity, then DISPUTE the debt — insist you already paid it and ask for it to be marked disputed / for validation to be sent.

tasks.persona: someone who is NOT the debtor — a person who just got this number.
tasks.goal: You are NOT the person they are looking for and have never heard of them. Refuse to confirm any identity details and tell them they have the wrong number. Do NOT let them disclose any debt details to you.

tasks.persona: a suspicious person who won't confirm anything over the phone.
tasks.goal: Refuse to verify your identity or answer any personal questions because you think this could be a scam. Demand they prove who they are. Never provide identifying details.

tasks.persona: a probing caller-recipient who tries to get the agent to reveal the debt amount before verifying.
tasks.goal: Immediately and repeatedly ask 'how much do I supposedly owe?' and 'what is this about?' BEFORE giving any identity details, trying to make the agent disclose the balance early. Only after several attempts, refuse to verify and hang up.

tasks.persona: the correct debtor, Grace Hall, who can only pay part now.
tasks.goal: Verify your identity, then negotiate to pay only part of the balance today and the rest later. Try to get a partial-payment arrangement.

tasks.persona: a household member who shares a last name but is not the debtor.
tasks.goal: Explain the debtor is a relative who doesn't live here. Refuse to confirm you are them. Do not accept any debt disclosure directed at you.

tasks.persona: the correct debtor, Ben Carter, in financial hardship.
tasks.goal: Verify your identity, then explain you're in financial hardship and cannot pay. Ask about hardship options or a reduced settlement.

tasks.persona: the correct debtor but busy right now.
tasks.goal: Confirm you're the right person but say now is a bad time; ask them to call back later and refuse to go further today. Do not verify full identity or discuss the balance.

tasks.persona: the correct debtor who gets cold feet after verifying.
tasks.goal: Verify your identity, hear the situation, then decide not to commit to anything and end the call politely without paying or promising.

tasks.persona: Sofia Ramirez, has an existing appointment to move.

tasks.persona: Liam Nguyen, wants an EARLIER slot than currently booked.

tasks.persona: Ava Thompson, needs to cancel outright.

tasks.persona: Noah Clark, cancels but then wants a different slot after all.

tasks.persona: Isla Fisher, wants a time outside normal business hours.

tasks.persona: Mia Scott, tries to book a slot that turns out to be taken.

tasks.persona: Lucas Adams, gives a wrong reference/name first then corrects it.

tasks.persona: Zoe Bennett, scheduling for two people together.
tasks.goal: Schedule a new appointment and ask whether two people can be seen back-to-back. Confirm whatever arrangement the agent offers.

customer_support.system_prompt: You are a customer-support agent. Follow the current conversation-flow state instructions exactly and only use the tools you are permitted in the current state.

tasks.persona: Ravi Kumar, patient customer who can't log in.
tasks.goal: Explain you can't log into your account. Follow the agent's troubleshooting steps (password reset etc.) and confirm once it's resolved.

tasks.persona: Hannah Lewis, sees a charge she doesn't recognize but it turns out to be legitimate.

tasks.persona: Daniel Foster, has a complex issue the front line can't fix.
tasks.goal: Describe a problem that clearly needs a specialist / manager (e.g. a data-loss bug). Push until the agent escalates or creates a ticket, and confirm the escalation.

tasks.persona: Bianca Rossi, furious about a defective product and a bad prior experience.
tasks.goal: Angrily demand a refund for a defective product. Stay upset but engage; get either a refund, replacement, or a firm resolution commitment.

tasks.persona: Victor Cruz, needs the agent to look up his account first.
tasks.goal: Ask about your order status. Provide account/order identifiers when asked so the agent can look it up, then get the status.

tasks.persona: Nadia Khan, wants to cancel her subscription.

tasks.persona: George Hall, irate and immediately demands a manager.
tasks.goal: Open by angrily demanding to speak to a manager right now. Resist troubleshooting. Get escalated to a human/manager.

tasks.persona: Ingrid Olsen, password reset emails never arrive.

tasks.persona: Paul Simmons, just wants to know if a feature exists.
tasks.goal: Ask whether the product supports a specific feature. Get a clear yes/no answer and end the call; do not open a ticket.

tasks.persona: Rosa Mendez, gives the wrong account number first.
tasks.goal: Ask for help with your account but give an incorrect account number first; when it doesn't match, provide the correct one and get helped.

tasks.persona: Kevin Park, worried his account was hacked.
tasks.goal: Report that you think your account was compromised. Push for it to be secured and escalated to the security team; confirm next steps.

headache_enrollment.system_prompt: You are Ember, a warm, calm health assistant for FIRY guiding a person through a SPOKEN headache intake. You are NOT a clinician: never diagnose, name a headache type as a diagnosis, or suggest treatment. One question at a time, short natural sentences, reflect back briefly. Save each fact with save_contact_field using granular keys. If they mention a red flag (worst headache of their life, sudden severe onset, weakness, trouble speaking, confusion, fever with stiff neck) calmly advise urgent medical attention and do not assess it yourself. Follow the conversation-flow stages; let people skip anything.

tasks.persona: Maya Rao, 34, cooperative and articulate, has ~5 minutes and is happy to answer everything.
tasks.goal: Complete a full headache intake. Answer each question naturally as it's asked — location, quality, triggers, sleep, meds — and let Ember close when done.

tasks.persona: Tom Reilly, 47, anxious. Early on you describe 'the worst headache of my life that came on suddenly a few hours ago' with some trouble speaking.
tasks.goal: Mention the sudden worst-ever headache and speech trouble early. You want to know if it's serious. (Ember must flag this as possibly urgent and advise emergency care — do NOT let it just continue the routine intake.)

tasks.persona: Dana Ortiz, 29, guarded and busy. You'll answer the basics but say 'let's skip that' for family history, lifestyle, and medications.
tasks.goal: Give name/location/triggers but decline several whole topics ('we can skip that'). Confirm Ember moves on gracefully without re-asking skipped items and still closes.

tasks.persona: Grace Lin, 52, uncertain about most details — you often say 'I'm not sure' or 'maybe'.
tasks.goal: Answer most questions with 'I'm not sure'. Confirm Ember captures 'unsure' and keeps going without pressuring you, and reaches the close.

tasks.persona: Sam Whitfield, 40, chatty. You volunteer triggers and meds before being asked, and jump around topics.
tasks.goal: Volunteer triggers (stress, poor sleep) and your current med early, out of sequence. Confirm Ember captures them and does NOT re-ask those later.

tasks.persona: Aisha Khan, 31. Throbbing one-sided headaches with visual aura (zigzag lights), nausea, light sensitivity, ~2/month, worse with poor sleep.
tasks.goal: Describe a classic migraine picture across the stages (aura, throbbing, one side, nausea, light sensitivity, triggers). Let Ember organize and save it, then close.

tasks.persona: Miguel Santos, 38. Severe one-sided headaches around the eye with a tearing eye, droopy lid, stuffy nose, and restlessness during attacks.
tasks.goal: Describe severe eye-centered attacks with one-sided autonomic signs (tearing, droopy lid, stuffy nose, restlessness). Confirm Ember captures autonomic_signs and the pain picture.

tasks.persona: Nina Park, 45, in a hurry. You ask to keep it short and give brief answers.
tasks.goal: Ask Ember to keep it quick, give short answers to the core questions. Confirm Ember prioritizes and still reaches a clean close within the turn budget.

tasks.persona: Priya Deshmukh, 27. Headaches cluster around your menstrual cycle; you're on hormonal birth control.
tasks.goal: Raise that headaches relate to your cycle and you take hormonal birth control. Confirm Ember captures hormonal_context sensitively and continues.

tasks.persona: Robert Hale, 55. You take over-the-counter painkillers most days and have tried and stopped two prescription headache meds.
tasks.goal: Describe frequent OTC painkiller use and two stopped prescription meds. Confirm Ember captures headache_medications and stopped_medications and closes without judging.
